{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Outsourcing Agreement (M&I)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the M&I Outsourcing Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Outsourcing Agreement. Of the eighteen rules assessed, thirteen are deviations requiring redlines and five are compliant as drafted.

The agreement is heavily weighted to M&I across the commercial exit and risk-allocation provisions. Four issues account for most of the exposure:

- **Liability (critical).** Section 13.4 caps only M&I's liability, at three months' payments, with no carve-outs and indemnities sitting inside the cap. This hits two walk-away triggers (one-sided cap; Vendor cap below six months' fees).
- **IP and Customer Data (critical).** Section 10.4 gives M&I sole ownership of works it creates in performing the Services, including work we pay for, and Section 17.2 confirms we receive no rights beyond use during the Term. Section 17.4 also permits M&I to use Customer Data for the broad "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" rather than solely to provide the Services.
- **Lock-in (high).** Section 10.3(A) requires us to source every Service in the Monthly Base Fee from M&I for the full eight-year Term, with no performance-based release; the Monthly Base Fee is a minimum payable in advance for that same period. Together these form an eight-year take-or-pay with no reduction right.
- **Exit economics (high/low).** Our only convenience exit requires a full year's notice plus a fee measured against the Estimated Remaining Value, and Section 13.5 characterises two Customer-payable fees as liquidated damages, one triggered by any Event of Default.

The compliant findings are genuinely clean: there is no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on us, no vendor audit right against us, no MFN obligation burdening us, and no automatic renewal (renewal is by mutual written agreement, and the only unilateral extension right runs in our favour).

Our redlines target the playbook fallback wherever a fallback cure is workable, and the preferred position only where the fallback is inadequate (exclusivity, non-solicitation) — in each case with the shortest surgical edit that avoids collateral rewrites.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | Redacted (§§ 10.4, 17.1, 17.2, 17.4 discussed) |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | § 13 (Damages) |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 22 (Miscellaneous Provisions) |
| 4 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Deviation | § 10 (Modification or Termination of Services) |
| 5 | High | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | Outsourcing Agreement (§ 14.2 discussed) |
| 6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 23 (Source Code) |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | **Compliant** | § 21.4 (Reliance on Data) |
| 8 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 11 (Termination) |
| 9 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Compliant** | § 21.4 (Reliance on Data) |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 22 (Miscellaneous Provisions) |
| 11 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | **Compliant** | § 8 (Fees) |
| 12 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Deviation | § 8 (Fees) |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Deviation | § 22 (Miscellaneous Provisions) |
| 14 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | **Compliant** | § 2 (Term) |
| 15 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Deviation | Redacted (§ 11.4 discussed) |
| 16 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 16.1 (By M&I) |
| 17 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Deviation | § 14 (Insurance and Indemnity) |
| 18 | Low | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Deviation | § 13 (Damages) |

### 2.1 Critical

**IP — ownership of deliverables and Customer Data (deviation).** Section 10.4 gives M&I sole ownership of all writings and works of authorship it creates in performing the Services, expressly including work paid for by us, with only a partial refund/credit if M&I later productises it. Section 17.2 confirms we have no rights in M&I materials beyond use "during the Term to process its data," so there is no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to the Developed Software and the fallback fails on its material terms. Separately, Section 17.4 permits use of Customer Data for the broad "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" rather than solely to provide the Services. *Proposal:* add a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence for us to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software, and limit M&I's Customer Data use to processing solely to provide the Services. We target the fallback rather than reversing ownership: M&I's retained ownership of programs, ideas and know-how is acceptable, and an assignment would require collateral rewrites of the 10.4 refund mechanic. Our ownership of Customer Data under 17.1 is favourable and is not flagged.

**LOL-CAP — limitation of liability (deviation).** Section 13.4 caps only M&I's liability, leaving us uncapped, at three months' payments and with no carve-outs; indemnities under Section 14.2 sit inside the cap with no super-cap. This hits two walk-away triggers — a one-sided cap and a Vendor cap below six months' fees. *Proposal:* edit the single capping sentence to the fallback — a mutual cap at twelve months' payments made to M&I, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct uncapped. The mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages in Section 13.2 is retained. Preferred extras (greater-of USD 1,000,000; data protection/security, fraud and IP carve-outs; payment-obligation exclusion) are not pursued at this level.

### 2.2 High

**ASSIGN (deviation).** Section 22.4 retains the mutual consent gate and the "not unreasonably withheld" standard but fails the fallback in three respects: our only consent-free route is a merger in which we are a party where the survivor becomes an Affiliate of a financial institution with capital and surplus of at least $100,000,000 (so a sale of substantially all assets, or a merger with a smaller acquirer, still needs M&I's consent, while M&I may "freely assign"); no written notice is required for a permitted successor assignment; and proviso (b) lets M&I escape the consent gate for transactions that are not successor transfers at all — a corporate reorganisation and a sale of the M&I Data Services division alone under (b)(ii), where M&I survives. *Proposal:* symmetrical successor carve-out for us, one mutual notice sentence tracking the existing (a)/(b) lettering, and narrowing of M&I's consent-free route to a true successor by merger or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities. The § 21.11 condition, the consent gate and the reasonableness standard are untouched. We do not pursue the preferred position (deleting M&I's free-assignment right and adding an affiliate carve-out and competitor bar). On change of control, § 21.11.B commits M&I to continue providing Services with no termination or re-pricing right (volume cap of pre-change levels plus 25%), and redacted § 11.3 is referenced in 11.1 as a Customer termination route excused from the Termination for Convenience Fee — both Customer benefits, neither flagged.

**EXCLUSIVITY (deviation, walk-away territory).** Section 10.3(A) is a de facto all-requirements commitment: we must obtain from M&I every Service included in the Monthly Base Fee "during the Term," defined as running to the eighth anniversary of the Commencement Date. There is no product-category limitation, no 12-month cap, and no automatic release on M&I's failure to meet the Performance Standards (Article 9) or delivery/processing deadlines, so all four fallback elements fail. Nothing cures it: §§ 21.10 and 21.11 merely define scope and pricing assumptions, and the § 1.1(C) recital is not an operative sourcing covenant. *Proposal:* one surgical replacement of the offending sentence removing the sourcing obligation and confirming M&I is a non-exclusive provider, leaving the pricing acknowledgment intact.

**INDEMN (deviation).** Section 14.2(B) already gives us an M&I indemnity with an express duty to defend for third-party IP infringement claims against the Services or M&I software, and § 14.3 supplies notice, assumption/control of the defence and cooperation; because the preamble defines "Customer" as Tri City National Bank "including its Affiliates," those obligations already run to our Affiliates. The bargain nevertheless fails the preferred checklist on two material points: M&I's indemnity does not reach M&I's violation of applicable law generally (only protected-class statutes are listed), M&I-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of our data, or M&I's gross negligence or wilful misconduct; and our own indemnity at 14.2(A) is sweeping (representations, protected-class laws, harassment, work injury, all property/financial loss from our acts or omissions, and § 6.6(B) matters). *Proposal:* a new operative Paragraph C adding the three missing conduct limbs, and a narrowing of Paragraph A to content we supply and our own violation of law. Noted but not flagged: the retained IP limb reaches only US patent, copyright and trademark claims (not trade-secret misappropriation or non-US rights); § 6.6 is "INTENTIONALLY OMITTED," so dropping limb (vi) leaves no orphaned reference; and the three-month cap is addressed under LOL-CAP, so the fallback's 3x annual fees super-cap is not pursued here.

**LICENSE (deviation).** The only licence granted to us is the Article 23 source code licence, expressly "non-transferable" and reinforced by the § 23.5 bar on transfer or assignment to any third party. That fails the fallback requirement of transferability to a successor in a merger or acquisition; the § 22.4 carve-out covers assignment of the Agreement only, and only where the surviving corporation joins a financial institution with $100,000,000 of capital and surplus. Affiliate coverage is already satisfied (defined "Customer" includes Affiliates; § 21.10 confirms Affiliate processing), so no duplicate wording was added. *Proposal:* a successor-transfer permission in the grant plus a conforming carve-out to the 23.5 restriction so the clauses do not contradict. We have not pressed the preferred position (contractor coverage; perpetual/irrevocable paid-up licence) given the term-limited escrow-release structure.

**NONCOMPETE (compliant).** No non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction binds us. Article 3 (Appointment) contains no exclusivity or requirements commitment; Article 2 (Term) is renewal-only; the only "compet-" hit is "court or arbitrator of competent jurisdiction" in § 22.10. Section 21.11 (Future Acquisitions) does not restrict our businesses — it contemplates new branches, new operations, acquisitions of Control of additional financial institutions and a Change in Control, and addresses only fees, conversion scheduling and the scope of M&I's continuing service obligation. Sections 21.7(B) and 23.5 are scope-of-licence/no-resale terms governing M&I's own Services and source code and fall outside this rule. Restrictions binding M&I are not flagged. No redline.

**T4C (deviation).** The Term runs eight years and our only convenience exit (11.1) requires a full year's notice plus a fee measured against the Estimated Remaining Value (all remaining months at the Monthly Base Fee or recent average fees), payable 50/50, plus uncapped unamortised Conversion costs and Expenses — failing the fallback on notice (far beyond 60–90 days) and charge (far beyond three months' fees). On the vendor side, § 10.2 lets M&I withdraw any non-Core Services "at any time" mid-term, a convenience right the fallback confines to the end of a term (its 90 days' notice already meets the notice floor). *Proposal:* Customer convenience termination on 90 days' notice with the fee capped at three months' Fees, and M&I service withdrawal limited to the end of the Term. We target the fallback rather than preferred because zeroing the fee would require collateral rewrites to 11.2(A) and the 13.5 liquidated-damages acknowledgement. Noted but not flagged: immediate withdrawal on a regulatory determination is condition-based rather than convenience, and the EFT services provision is triggered by loss of network access.

### 2.3 Medium

**AUDIT (compliant).** No audit, inspection, verification or usage-monitoring right runs against us. Every audit/examination provision runs the other way or is regulator-driven and benefits us: § 21.8(C) obliges M&I to procure an annual independent third-party review of its own Operations Center and give us the report free of charge; §§ 21.8(B) and 17.1 subject M&I-held records and Customer Data to examination by our regulators and auditors; § 21.8 subjects M&I's performance to examination by our regulatory agencies. Section 21.7(C) is only a books-and-records reflection covenant with evidence on request. M&I has no direct access to our systems for audit purposes. No redline.

**GOVLAW (deviation).** Section 22.1 selects Wisconsin internal law and § 22.2 fixes exclusive venue in the courts of Milwaukee County and the Eastern District of Wisconsin. Wisconsin is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), so the fallback governing-law and forum elements fail on their material terms. This is not walk-away territory: disputes go to court, Article 15 provides only a non-binding executive escalation (the arbitration references in 22.2 and 22.11 are incidental), and the venue is domestic. *Proposal:* replace only the jurisdiction and forum words with New York law and the New York County courts, leaving the conflict-of-laws exclusion, the judgment-enforcement sentence and all other wording intact. Delaware or California law and courts remain an acceptable fallback.

**MFN (compliant).** Searches for most-favoured-nation, best/lowest price, "no less favorable" terms, comparable-customer pricing and right-to-match mechanics returned no hits; §§ 8 and 3 confirm pricing is fixed solely by the Fee Schedule with no obligation on us to extend M&I terms given to third parties or to match third-party offers. There is also no MFN in our favour, a nice-to-have only under this rule, noted rather than redlined.

**MINCOMMIT (deviation, walk-away territory).** The Monthly Base Fee is a minimum monthly fee payable in advance for the entire eight-year Term, and we must source the whole bundled Service set from M&I for the Term. Nothing permits reduction of the minimum; the only relief is a good-faith renegotiation if M&I itself withdraws a bundled Service. *Proposal:* limit the commitment to the current twelve-month period, allow reduction on thirty days' notice, and settle any shortfall by a true-up rather than a penalty. Termination fee mechanics are left to the termination-for-convenience rule.

**NOSOLICIT (deviation, walk-away territory).** Section 22.14 binds us not to solicit any M&I employee, for any reason, for the entire eight-year Term. That fails the fallback on three material terms: it is not limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, it far exceeds 12 months from the end of a person's involvement, and there is no carve-out for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches. A restriction longer than 24 months covering all Vendor personnel is walk-away territory. It does stop short of a no-hire (solicitation only). *Proposal:* the shortest edit to the preferred position — make § 22.14 one-way, so M&I remains restricted from soliciting our employees while no non-solicitation restriction binds us.

**RENEWAL (compliant).** No automatic renewal. Section 2.1 provides a fixed initial Term "unless extended or earlier terminated," and § 2.2 makes any renewal dependent on M&I's written proposal and our written agreement to renewal terms — renewal only by mutual written agreement, which meets the preferred position. The conditional preferred elements (12-month renewal term, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder) and price-uplift caps are not engaged: there is no unilateral Vendor uplift mechanic and no non-renewal notice window is imposed on us (silence simply lets the Term expire). The only unilateral extension right runs in our favour — a single twelve-month extension "at the then-current terms and conditions," i.e. no price increase. The 18-month M&I proposal lead time and the 5-month deadline for exercising our option are noted, benefit us, and are not redlined.

**TRANSITION (deviation).** Section 11.4 supplies Termination Assistance on expiry or any termination for any reason and confirms charging at M&I's then-current rates, but fails the fallback on two material terms. First, the only quantified assistance period (six months of continued Services) is conditioned on a written request given at least 100 days before expiration of the Term, so it is unavailable after a mid-term termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination assistance duration. Second, nothing obliges M&I to return or export Customer Data — § 17.1 confirms our ownership and § 17.5 addresses only safeguards. *Proposal:* insert a fallback-level clause giving at least 90 days of Termination Assistance after any expiry or termination plus a 30-day Customer Data export, leaving the existing six-month expiry mechanic and then-current-rates basis untouched.

**WARRANTY (deviation).** Section 16.1 contains only a systems-capability representation (A), a promise that reports will substantially conform to customer bulletins and User Manuals (B), rights and authority reps and a Millennium compliance rep, all wrapped by an all-other-warranties disclaimer in 16.1.F. A report-to-manual conformity promise is not a software-to-documentation warranty, and no provision (16.1, § 9 Performance Standards, § 12.3 remedies or § 13 Damages) gives repair, replacement or refund for non-conforming software or Services; the Service Level Credits at 9.2.D are redacted. Section 9.1 does commit M&I to perform the Services in accordance with the Performance Standards for the whole term, satisfying the fallback services-duration element. *Proposal:* add a 90-day software conformance warranty and repair/replace/refund remedy as a new § 16.1.G, which the "EXCEPT AS SPECIFICALLY SET FORTH IN THIS SECTION 16.1" disclaimer preserves without further edits.

### 2.4 Low

**INSURANCE (deviation).** Section 14.1 contains a real insurance clause (CGL at $2,000,000 primary limits, fidelity $10,000,000, workers' compensation as mandated by the state, all-risk property, plus "A"-rated carriers, 30 days' notice of change/cancellation and certificates on request), but no professional liability (E&O) and no cyber/privacy coverage — failing both fallback elements for a vendor that processes our data and Items. *Proposal:* add only those two coverages ($1,000,000 E&O; $2,000,000 cyber/privacy) as a new item in the 14.1(A) schedule, so the existing at-own-expense lead-in, notice and certificate mechanics in 14.1(B) apply unchanged. Preferred-level limits (E&O $2M, cyber $5M) are noted but not pressed.

**LD (deviation, approaching walk-away).** Section 13.5 expressly characterises two Customer-payable fees as liquidated damages, each quantified as a percentage of the Estimated Remaining Value under §§ 11.1 and 11.2(A), with the Termination for Cause Fee triggered by any Event of Default. That fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages) and the fallback (a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees). Deleting the fees outright would require collateral rewrites of the exit mechanics, so we cure at the fallback: 11.1 caps the fee at three months of Fees and its applicability sentence is conformed to cross-refer to 11.2(A) (removing the Customer-default carve-out that would otherwise contradict amended 11.2(A)); 11.2(A) applies that same single fee instead of a separate remaining-value cause fee; and 13.5 confirms it is the sole liquidated amount payable by us. Notice periods, instalment timing and the existing 13.4 carve-out are untouched. Worth raising commercially (not a checklist element): the fee remains payable on any Customer Event of Default, however minor, so a materiality/cure qualifier would further close that concern.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These findings sit in, or approach, walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating preferences.

1. **One-sided, sub-six-month liability cap — § 13 (Damages).** Section 13.4 caps M&I alone at three months' payments with no carve-outs; two independent walk-away triggers. Must move to a mutual twelve-month cap with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct uncapped.
2. **Eight-year exclusive dealing with no performance exit — § 10.3(A).** All-requirements sourcing for the full Term, no category limit, no 12-month cap and no release on failure to meet the Performance Standards.
3. **Eight-year take-or-pay minimum with no reduction right — § 8 (Fees).** Monthly Base Fee payable in advance for the whole Term, reducible only by good-faith renegotiation if M&I itself withdraws a Service.
4. **Term-length, all-personnel non-solicitation binding us — § 22.14.** Eight years, all M&I employees, no involvement limitation and no general-advertisement carve-out; exceeds the 24-month walk-away threshold.
5. **Remaining-value liquidated damages payable by us — § 13.5 with §§ 11.1 and 11.2(A).** Percentage-of-Estimated-Remaining-Value fees, one triggered by any Event of Default; approaching walk-away and closely tied to the § 11.1 convenience-exit economics.

Items 1 and 3 also interact with the critical IP position: without a perpetual licence to the Developed Software (§§ 10.4, 17.2) and with Customer Data use untethered from service provision (§ 17.4), the lock-in has no offsetting exit value.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline.** Thirteen deviations have drafted proposals; all verified (three repaired: ASSIGN, INDEMN, LD). We recommend a single consolidated markup rather than sequential exchanges.
2. **Sequence the negotiation.** Lead with the five walk-away items (LOL-CAP, EXCLUSIVITY, MINCOMMIT, NOSOLICIT, LD) plus IP, and hold the medium and low items (GOVLAW, TRANSITION, WARRANTY, INSURANCE) as a closing package.
3. **Confirm internal positions before the call.** We need business sign-off on (a) the twelve-month mutual cap and the uncapped carve-out list; (b) willingness to accept fallback-level exit economics (90 days' notice, three months' Fees) versus pressing for no fee; and (c) whether a 12-month reducible minimum matches the forecast volumes.
4. **Flag the drafting dependencies to the deal team.** The T4C and LD cures are interlocking (§§ 11.1, 11.2(A), 13.4, 13.5); any concession on one must be checked against the others. The IP cure is deliberately a licence rather than an assignment to avoid reopening the § 10.4 refund mechanic.
5. **Raise commercially, outside the checklist.** Seek a materiality and cure qualifier on the Customer Event of Default trigger for the termination fee; note also that the retained IP indemnity limb covers only US patent, copyright and trademark claims and not trade-secret or non-US rights, and that the § 9.2.D Service Level Credits are redacted and should be produced before we finalise the warranty and remedies position.
6. **Preserve the favourable terms.** No renewal, no vendor audit right, no MFN and no non-compete binding us are all confirmed compliant; the § 21.11.B change-of-control continuation obligation, the redacted § 11.3 termination route, our Customer Data ownership under § 17.1 and our unilateral twelve-month extension at then-current terms all run in our favour and should not be reopened."}

There is no product-category limitation, no 12-month cap, and no automatic release on M&I's failure to meet the Performance Standards (Article 9) or delivery/processing deadlines, so all four fallback elements fail. Nothing cures it: §§ 21.10 and 21.11 merely define scope and pricing assumptions, and the § 1.1(C) recital is not an operative sourcing covenant. *Proposal:* one surgical replacement of the offending sentence removing the sourcing obligation and confirming M&I is a non-exclusive provider, leaving the pricing acknowledgment intact.

**INDEMN (deviation).** Section 14.2(B) already gives us an M&I indemnity with an express duty to defend for third-party IP infringement claims against the Services or M&I software, and § 14.3 supplies notice, assumption/control of the defence and cooperation; because the preamble defines "Customer" as Tri City National Bank "including its Affiliates," those obligations already run to our Affiliates. The bargain nevertheless fails the preferred checklist on two material points: M&I's indemnity does not reach M&I's violation of applicable law generally (only protected-class statutes are listed), M&I-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of our data, or M&I's gross negligence or wilful misconduct; and our own indemnity at 14.2(A) is sweeping (representations, protected-class laws, harassment, work injury, all property/financial loss from our acts or omissions, and § 6.6(B) matters). *Proposal:* a new operative Paragraph C adding the three missing conduct limbs, and a narrowing of Paragraph A to content we supply and our own violation of law. Noted but not flagged: the retained IP limb reaches only US patent, copyright and trademark claims (not trade-secret misappropriation or non-US rights); § 6.6 is "INTENTIONALLY OMITTED," so dropping limb (vi) leaves no orphaned reference; and the three-month cap is addressed under LOL-CAP, so the fallback's 3x annual fees super-cap is not pursued here.

**LICENSE (deviation).** The only licence granted to us is the Article 23 source code licence, expressly "non-transferable" and reinforced by the § 23.5 bar on transfer or assignment to any third party. That fails the fallback requirement of transferability to a successor in a merger or acquisition; the § 22.4 carve-out covers assignment of the Agreement only, and only where the surviving corporation joins a financial institution with $100,000,000 of capital and surplus. Affiliate coverage is already satisfied (defined "Customer" includes Affiliates; § 21.10 confirms Affiliate processing), so no duplicate wording was added. *Proposal:* a successor-transfer permission in the grant plus a conforming carve-out to the 23.5 restriction so the clauses do not contradict. We have not pressed the preferred position (contractor coverage; perpetual/irrevocable paid-up licence) given the term-limited escrow-release structure.

**NONCOMPETE (compliant).** No non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction binds us. Article 3 (Appointment) contains no exclusivity or requirements commitment; Article 2 (Term) is renewal-only; the only "compet-" hit is "court or arbitrator of competent jurisdiction" in § 22.10. Section 21.11 (Future Acquisitions) does not restrict our businesses — it contemplates new branches, new operations, acquisitions of Control of additional financial institutions and a Change in Control, and addresses only fees, conversion scheduling and the scope of M&I's continuing service obligation. Sections 21.7(B) and 23.5 are scope-of-licence/no-resale terms governing M&I's own Services and source code and fall outside this rule. Restrictions binding M&I are not flagged. No redline.

**T4C (deviation).** The Term runs eight years and our only convenience exit (11.1) requires a full year's notice plus a fee measured against the Estimated Remaining Value (all remaining months at the Monthly Base Fee or recent average fees), payable 50/50, plus uncapped unamortised Conversion costs and Expenses — failing the fallback on notice (far beyond 60–90 days) and charge (far beyond three months' fees). On the vendor side, § 10.2 lets M&I withdraw any non-Core Services "at any time" mid-term, a convenience right the fallback confines to the end of a term (its 90 days' notice already meets the notice floor). *Proposal:* Customer convenience termination on 90 days' notice with the fee capped at three months' Fees, and M&I service withdrawal limited to the end of the Term. We target the fallback rather than preferred because zeroing the fee would require collateral rewrites to 11.2(A) and the 13.5 liquidated-damages acknowledgement. Noted but not flagged: immediate withdrawal on a regulatory determination is condition-based rather than convenience, and the EFT services provision is triggered by loss of network access.

### 2.3 Medium

**AUDIT (compliant).** No audit, inspection, verification or usage-monitoring right runs against us. Every audit/examination provision runs the other way or is regulator-driven and benefits us: § 21.8(C) obliges M&I to procure an annual independent third-party review of its own Operations Center and give us the report free of charge; §§ 21.8(B) and 17.1 subject M&I-held records and Customer Data to examination by our regulators and auditors; § 21.8 subjects M&I's performance to examination by our regulatory agencies. Section 21.7(C) is only a books-and-records reflection covenant with evidence on request. M&I has no direct access to our systems for audit purposes. No redline.

**GOVLAW (deviation).** Section 22.1 selects Wisconsin internal law and § 22.2 fixes exclusive venue in the courts of Milwaukee County and the Eastern District of Wisconsin. Wisconsin is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), so the fallback governing-law and forum elements fail on their material terms. This is not walk-away territory: disputes go to court, Article 15 provides only a non-binding executive escalation (the arbitration references in 22.2 and 22.11 are incidental), and the venue is domestic. *Proposal:* replace only the jurisdiction and forum words with New York law and the New York County courts, leaving the conflict-of-laws exclusion, the judgment-enforcement sentence and all other wording intact. Delaware or California law and courts remain an acceptable fallback.

**MFN (compliant).** Searches for most-favoured-nation, best/lowest price, "no less favorable" terms, comparable-customer pricing and right-to-match mechanics returned no hits; §§ 8 and 3 confirm pricing is fixed solely by the Fee Schedule with no obligation on us to extend M&I terms given to third parties or to match third-party offers. There is also no MFN in our favour, a nice-to-have only under this rule, noted rather than redlined.

**MINCOMMIT (deviation, walk-away territory).** The Monthly Base Fee is a minimum monthly fee payable in advance for the entire eight-year Term, and we must source the whole bundled Service set from M&I for the Term. Nothing permits reduction of the minimum; the only relief is a good-faith renegotiation if M&I itself withdraws a bundled Service. *Proposal:* limit the commitment to the current twelve-month period, allow reduction on thirty days' notice, and settle any shortfall by a true-up rather than a penalty. Termination fee mechanics are left to the termination-for-convenience rule.

**NOSOLICIT (deviation, walk-away territory).** Section 22.14 binds us not to solicit any M&I employee, for any reason, for the entire eight-year Term. That fails the fallback on three material terms: it is not limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, it far exceeds 12 months from the end of a person's involvement, and there is no carve-out for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches. A restriction longer than 24 months covering all Vendor personnel is walk-away territory. It does stop short of a no-hire (solicitation only). *Proposal:* the shortest edit to the preferred position — make § 22.14 one-way, so M&I remains restricted from soliciting our employees while no non-solicitation restriction binds us.

**RENEWAL (compliant).** No automatic renewal. Section 2.1 provides a fixed initial Term "unless extended or earlier terminated," and § 2.2 makes any renewal dependent on M&I's written proposal and our written agreement to renewal terms — renewal only by mutual written agreement, which meets the preferred position. The conditional preferred elements (12-month renewal term, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder) and price-uplift caps are not engaged: there is no unilateral Vendor uplift mechanic and no non-renewal notice window is imposed on us (silence simply lets the Term expire). The only unilateral extension right runs in our favour — a single twelve-month extension "at the then-current terms and conditions," i.e. no price increase. The 18-month M&I proposal lead time and the 5-month deadline for exercising our option are noted, benefit us, and are not redlined.

**TRANSITION (deviation).** Section 11.4 supplies Termination Assistance on expiry or any termination for any reason and confirms charging at M&I's then-current rates, but fails the fallback on two material terms. First, the only quantified assistance period (six months of continued Services) is conditioned on a written request given at least 100 days before expiration of the Term, so it is unavailable after a mid-term termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination assistance duration. Second, nothing obliges M&I to return or export Customer Data — § 17.1 confirms our ownership and § 17.5 addresses only safeguards. *Proposal:* insert a fallback-level clause giving at least 90 days of Termination Assistance after any expiry or termination plus a 30-day Customer Data export, leaving the existing six-month expiry mechanic and then-current-rates basis untouched.

**WARRANTY (deviation).** Section 16.1 contains only a systems-capability representation (A), a promise that reports will substantially conform to customer bulletins and User Manuals (B), rights and authority reps and a Millennium compliance rep, all wrapped by an all-other-warranties disclaimer in 16.1.F. A report-to-manual conformity promise is not a software-to-documentation warranty, and no provision (16.1, § 9 Performance Standards, § 12.3 remedies or § 13 Damages) gives repair, replacement or refund for non-conforming software or Services; the Service Level Credits at 9.2.D are redacted. Section 9.1 does commit M&I to perform the Services in accordance with the Performance Standards for the whole term, satisfying the fallback services-duration element. *Proposal:* add a 90-day software conformance warranty and repair/replace/refund remedy as a new § 16.1.G, which the "EXCEPT AS SPECIFICALLY SET FORTH IN THIS SECTION 16.1" disclaimer preserves without further edits.

### 2.4 Low

**INSURANCE (deviation).** Section 14.1 contains a real insurance clause (CGL at $2,000,000 primary limits, fidelity $10,000,000, workers' compensation as mandated by the state, all-risk property, plus "A"-rated carriers, 30 days' notice of change/cancellation and certificates on request), but no professional liability (E&O) and no cyber/privacy coverage — failing both fallback elements for a vendor that processes our data and Items. *Proposal:* add only those two coverages ($1,000,000 E&O; $2,000,000 cyber/privacy) as a new item in the 14.1(A) schedule, so the existing at-own-expense lead-in, notice and certificate mechanics in 14.1(B) apply unchanged. Preferred-level limits (E&O $2M, cyber $5M) are noted but not pressed.

**LD (deviation, approaching walk-away).** Section 13.5 expressly characterises two Customer-payable fees as liquidated damages, each quantified as a percentage of the Estimated Remaining Value under §§ 11.1 and 11.2(A), with the Termination for Cause Fee triggered by any Event of Default. That fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages) and the fallback (a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees). Deleting the fees outright would require collateral rewrites of the exit mechanics, so we cure at the fallback: 11.1 caps the fee at three months of Fees and its applicability sentence is conformed to cross-refer to 11.2(A) (removing the Customer-default carve-out that would otherwise contradict amended 11.2(A)); 11.2(A) applies that same single fee instead of a separate remaining-value cause fee; and 13.5 confirms it is the sole liquidated amount payable by us. Notice periods, instalment timing and the existing 13.4 carve-out are untouched. Worth raising commercially (not a checklist element): the fee remains payable on any Customer Event of Default, however minor, so a materiality/cure qualifier would further close that concern.

## 3. Walk-away items

These findings sit in, or approach, walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating preferences.

1. **One-sided, sub-six-month liability cap — § 13 (Damages).** Section 13.4 caps M&I alone at three months' payments with no carve-outs; two independent walk-away triggers. Must move to a mutual twelve-month cap with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct uncapped.
2. **Eight-year exclusive dealing with no performance exit — § 10.3(A).** All-requirements sourcing for the full Term, no category limit, no 12-month cap and no release on failure to meet the Performance Standards.
3. **Eight-year take-or-pay minimum with no reduction right — § 8 (Fees).** Monthly Base Fee payable in advance for the whole Term, reducible only by good-faith renegotiation if M&I itself withdraws a Service.
4. **Term-length, all-personnel non-solicitation binding us — § 22.14.** Eight years, all M&I employees, no involvement limitation and no general-advertisement carve-out; exceeds the 24-month walk-away threshold.
5. **Remaining-value liquidated damages payable by us — § 13.5 with §§ 11.1 and 11.2(A).** Percentage-of-Estimated-Remaining-Value fees, one triggered by any Event of Default; approaching walk-away and closely tied to the § 11.1 convenience-exit economics.

Items 1 and 3 also interact with the critical IP position: without a perpetual licence to the Developed Software (§§ 10.4, 17.2) and with Customer Data use untethered from service provision (§ 17.4), the lock-in has no offsetting exit value.

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline.** Thirteen deviations have drafted proposals; all verified (three repaired: ASSIGN, INDEMN, LD). We recommend a single consolidated markup rather than sequential exchanges.
2. **Sequence the negotiation.** Lead with the five walk-away items (LOL-CAP, EXCLUSIVITY, MINCOMMIT, NOSOLICIT, LD) plus IP, and hold the medium and low items (GOVLAW, TRANSITION, WARRANTY, INSURANCE) as a closing package.
3. **Confirm internal positions before the call.** We need business sign-off on (a) the twelve-month mutual cap and the uncapped carve-out list; (b) willingness to accept fallback-level exit economics (90 days' notice, three months' Fees) versus pressing for no fee; and (c) whether a 12-month reducible minimum matches the forecast volumes.
4. **Flag the drafting dependencies to the deal team.** The T4C and LD cures are interlocking (§§ 11.1, 11.2(A), 13.4, 13.5); any concession on one must be checked against the others. The IP cure is deliberately a licence rather than an assignment to avoid reopening the § 10.4 refund mechanic.
5. **Raise commercially, outside the checklist.** Seek a materiality and cure qualifier on the Customer Event of Default trigger for the termination fee; note also that the retained IP indemnity limb covers only US patent, copyright and trademark claims and not trade-secret or non-US rights, and that the § 9.2.D Service Level Credits are redacted and should be produced before we finalise the warranty and remedies position.
6. **Preserve the favourable terms.** No renewal, no vendor audit right, no MFN and no non-compete binding us are all confirmed compliant; the § 21.11.B change-of-control continuation obligation, the redacted § 11.3 termination route, our Customer Data ownership under § 17.1 and our unilateral twelve-month extension at then-current terms all run in our favour and should not be reopened.
